senses.gloss: (b. h.; cmp. preced.) to be restless, flee.

units: <cite ref="Berakhot 19a:10">Ber. 19ᵃ</cite> <he>את מי נִדּוּ</he> whom did they (the scholars) excommunicate? <cite ref="Berakhot 19a:7">Ib.</cite> <he>ב״ד מְנַדִּין על כבוד הרב</he> the court proclaims the ban to protect a teacher’s authority.

<cite ref="Pesachim 52a:3">Pes. 52ᵃ</cite> <he>מנדין על שני וכ׳</he> we excommunicate for disregarding the second Holy Day observed in the diaspora; a. v. fr.—[<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 287">Yalk. Is. 287</cite> <he>נדית עלי</he>, v. <cite ref="N00234"><he>נִדְּנֵד</he></cite>.]—Part. pass. <he>מְנוּדֶּה</he>; pl. <he>מְנוּדִּין</he>.
<cite ref="Moed Katan 15a:21">M. Kat. 15ᵃ</cite> <he>מנ׳ לשמים</he> one excommunicated by the Lord, i.e. a mourner.

<cite ref="Moed Katan 15a:21">Ib.</cite> <he>מנ׳ מהו בד״ת</he> dare an excommunicated person study the Law? <cite ref="Moed Katan 15a:23">Ib.</cite> <he>מנ׳ מהו בקריעה</he> must an excommunicated person rend his garments? <cite ref="Mishnah Nedarim 1:1">Ned. I, 1</cite> <he>מנ׳ אני לך</he> I vow to be excommunicated towards thee, i.e. I vow not to receive any favors at thy hands.
<cite ref="Moed Katan 17a:1">M. Kat. 17ᵃ</cite> <he>מנ׳ לרב מנ׳ לתלמיד</he> one excommunicated by a teacher must be treated as such by his disciple (the latter cannot raise the ban).
<cite ref="Moed Katan 17a:17">Ib.</cite> <he>מנ׳ לעירו</he> one excommunicated by the authorities of his own city.
<cite ref="Moed Katan 15b:16">Ib. 15ᵇ</cite> <he>כל אותן שנים … מנ׳ היו</he> during all the years the Israelites were in the wilderness, they were excommunicated (by the Lord); a. v. fr.
<cite ref="Mishnah Eduyot 5:6">Eduy. V, 6</cite> <he>ח״ו שעקביא נ׳</he> God forbid (to say) that ‘A. was excommunicated.
<cite ref="Mishnah Eduyot 5:6">Ib.</cite> <he>כל המִתְנַדֶּה ומת וכ׳</he> he who dies while under excommunication has a stone placed on his coffin; a. fr.
